title: RepSNS Master Plan: 3-day full-body strength and muscle
summary: Your main plan. Three full-body sessions a week (Monday, Wednesday, Saturday), about 60 minutes each. Each day pairs a main lower-body lift with upper-body push and pull work. Every working set ends when the watch buzzes at its velocity-loss target or when you reach the top of the rep range. Monday and Saturday are the heavier days and Wednesday is a little lighter so you recover between them.
assumptions: Intermediate lifter, at least 6 months of regular training
Full gym: barbell, Smith machine, leg press, cables, pull-up bar, dumbbells
About 60 minutes per session including warm-up and rest
Goal: build strength and muscle at the same time
velocity_loss_explainer: Your watch measures how fast each rep moves. Your first reps set the baseline. When a rep is slower than the baseline by the target percentage (20%, 40% or 60%), the watch buzzes and the set is done. A higher percentage means more fatigue and a set closer to failure. 0 means the watch doesn't track that exercise.

days.name: Monday
days.focus: Full body: squat and horizontal push

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.notes: Under 6 reps: drop the weight. Over 10: add 5 kg.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.notes: Keep the bar close to your legs. Over 10 reps: add 5 kg.

exercises.name: Weighted pull-up
exercises.notes: Use bodyweight until you get 10 reps, then add 2.5 kg.

exercises.name: Cable lateral raise
exercises.notes: Not tracked by the watch. Stop 1-2 reps before failure.

days.cooldown: 3 min easy walk, light hip flexor and chest stretch

days.name: Wednesday
days.focus: Full body: lighter, speed and back

exercises.name: Back squat
exercises.notes: Move every rep fast. Over 6 reps: add 5 kg.

exercises.name: Chest-to-bar pull-up
exercises.notes: Skill work. Not tracked, focus on speed.

exercises.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
exercises.notes: Over 12 reps: add 2 kg per dumbbell.

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
exercises.notes: Lighter day: stop early and keep the reps crisp.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raise
exercises.notes: Not tracked by the watch. Slow and controlled.

days.cooldown: 3 min easy walk, light lat and hamstring stretch

days.name: Saturday
days.focus: Full body: hinge and vertical pull

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.notes: Under 6 reps: drop the weight. Over 10: add 5 kg.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
exercises.notes: Over 12 reps: add 2 kg per dumbbell.

exercises.name: Cable triceps pushdown + curl
exercises.notes: Not tracked by the watch. Do one set of each back to back.

days.cooldown: 3 min easy walk, light hip flexor and shoulder stretch

progression_rules: Can't reach the bottom of the rep range on working sets? Drop the weight if you were well short, or repeat the same weight next time.
Over the top of the rep range before the watch buzzes? Add 5 kg on lower-body exercises and 2.5 kg on upper-body exercises next session.
Rest 3 minutes between sets on the main lifts and 1-2 minutes on smaller exercises.
Keep the warm-up sets light. They prepare you; they shouldn't tire you.

block_weeks.focus: Learn the VL buzz and the lifts, leave reps in reserve
Use the targets in the tables
Add one set to the first lift of each day
Hardest week: push the main lifts slightly further
Lighter week to recover, then start again from week 2

adaptations: No limitations were given. If an exercise causes pain, stop it and ask the AI coach for a swap; check anything persistent with a professional.

pre_workout: Eat a normal meal with carbs and some protein 2-3 hours before, or a small carb snack (a banana, toast) 30-60 minutes before.
Coffee 30-60 minutes before is optional if it agrees with you.
post_workout: Have a meal with protein (around 20-40 g) and carbs within a few hours.
Total daily protein matters more than exact timing.
nutrition.hydration: Drink water through the day and sip during the session. Add electrolytes if you sweat heavily.

clarifying_questions: Do Monday, Wednesday and Saturday still suit you?
Any exercises that cause pain or that you dislike?
What is your main goal for the next 6 weeks?
